short_answer: Marco D'Angelo is a real, well known Las Vegas name. WagerTalk's own press releases call him a co founder of WagerTalk: in August 2018 he was quoted as "Co-Founder, WagerTalk.com" when WagerTalk bought SportsMemo, and in August 2019 as one of three hosts of its Bet On It football podcast. He sells his picks through WagerTalk and the partner site StatSalt. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money is a separate question. His profile leads with "#1 NBA CAPPER SINCE 2020 AT WAGERTALK" and "58-36 ON 5% MAJOR WAGERS SINCE 2024", but those rankings and records come from the company he helped start, which also sells the picks. WagerTalk's public leaderboard address returned an error, so we could not check the long term rankings at all.

What we could check came out mixed. His Last 20 on 20 Nov 2026 counted to 13 wins, 6 losses and 1 no play. His 5% Major Wager line, compared with an earlier WagerTalk figure reposted in April 2026, suggests those plays have been roughly even since then. The same 7 day record showed different dollar figures on WagerTalk and StatSalt on the same day.

Independent buyer talk is close to nonexistent. A Reddit member listed him among paid picks he follows in 2025, and TheRX lists him by name among services members should not post. Treat him as an established seller with in house rankings, not a proven winner, and record every pick yourself before buying a long pass.

guarantee: WagerTalk offers a paid "Pick Guarantee" option. Its wording on his profile: "The WagerTalk pick guarantee option backs your purchase with 100% in credits." If "your daily pick(s) package does not result in an overall profit across all included plays", then "the paid cash value of a guaranteed pick will be credited back to your account to be used on a future purchase."

That is store credit, not a refund, and it costs extra. On 17 Nov 2026 a single play listed at $25.00 cost $38.00 with the guarantee; on 20 Nov no guarantee price was shown on the profile. The wording covers daily pick packages; we found no guarantee wording on the multi day or season passes.
Betting losses on the picks are never covered, and they are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: How we checked: we read his WagerTalk profile, the WagerTalk experts page and StatSalt on 20 Nov 2026, counted the Last 20 results ourselves, recomputed every percentage from the wins and losses shown, and compared the 5% Major Wager line with the figure WagerTalk promoted in April 2026.

The rankings measure him against other WagerTalk sellers, on WagerTalk's own grading. WagerTalk's 2018 and 2019 press releases name him a co founder, so the board that ranks him belongs to a company he helped start.

Each run starts on a date chosen by the seller: since 2020, since 2021, since 2024, the last 17 college football 5% plays. A window picked after the fact tells you little. Where we could compare two seller figures for the same plays, the more recent stretch was weaker than the headline.
The 2010 baseball streak note says he never laid more than -120 in the 25 plays. We could not open any Sports Monitor record to confirm it.
record: Watchdog graded sample, new 22 Nov 2026. Marco D'Angelo does not publish a complete, time stamped log we can audit, so we built a sample from public posts that carry their plays. Watchdog captures X accounts and forum threads that post or repost picks; the ones naming Marco D'Angelo most often were BuzzKill (TheRX newsletters thread), WagerTalkPicks, 1218Sports, TheGodOfCappers. From 17 Oct 2026 to 24 Oct 2026 we took every play our parser could read inside a Marco D'Angelo block, kept only those posted before the game started, removed repeats, and graded each one against the final score at one unit risked, at the odds shown or -110 when none were shown.
Result: 2 plays, 1 won, 1 lost, -0.09 units, a return of -4.5% per unit risked. By sport: too few per sport to split. By month: October 1 won, 1 lost, -0.09 units.

What it means: 2 decided plays is far too few to judge. We list them so readers can see what was posted and how it did; the sample covers only plays others chose to post, not the full card a subscriber receives.
What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every Marco D'Angelo pick from an outside tracker, and no court or regulator record about him.

What WagerTalk publishes: a Last 20 list on his profile, which we counted at 13 wins, 6 losses and 1 no play on 20 Nov 2026 (12, 7 and 1 on 17 Nov), plus 3, 7 and 30 day Who's Hot boards. On 20 Nov he led the all sports 7 day board at 11-6-0 for $1,887 and also showed on two sport boards at 3-1 and 2-1. These are graded by the company that sells the picks, so they are marketing, not an audit.

Background: WagerTalk's August 2019 release describes him as "a professional sports handicapper and bettor since 1980" and a WagerTalk co founder who makes regional and national media appearances. His bio says he moved to Las Vegas in 2008 and co hosted a Las Vegas radio show. On 17 Nov 2026 SportsMemo, also owned by WagerTalk, sold his game of the week and a 7 day pass; on 20 Nov he was not on the SportsMemo experts list.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on Marco D'Angelo is thin. We found no buyer review of a paid package, good or bad. Reddit archive searches for his name timed out or were rate limited again on 20 Nov 2026, so we relied on our saved copy of ten betting subreddits from January 2024 to November 2026, which matched only the two posts below. Here is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found six items on five sites, from 2025 and 2026, and none is a review of a paid package. A Reddit member listed him among paid picks they follow in February 2025, with a running count of 31 and 13. A TheRX member reposted WagerTalk's claim of a 5 and 0 March 2026 on his 5% plays, while the same forum's rules name him, and all WagerTalk cappers, as services members should not post. On Sportsbook Review one member praised WagerTalk's free odds screen but called its picks side a tout site. CapperTek's 14 WagerTalk reviews from 2021 to 2026 are almost all negative about the site's handicappers and records in general, but none names him. We found no complaint and no buyer praise specific to his paid picks, so there is no smoke either way; there is simply very little talk.

WagerTalk's Who's Hot boards put him first on the all sports 7 day board at 11-6-0 for $1,887, and near the top of two sport boards. StatSalt's board showed the same week as 11-6 for $1,787. WagerTalk grades and sells the picks, and its releases call him a co founder, so this is not independent evidence.

On r/sportsbetting, a member who posts the paid picks they follow listed Marco D'Angelo with a count of 31 and 13 and a game of the week listed as "Kent 1.5". Their second list that day showed 31 and 14. The posts had no replies and do not say how the count was kept.

In a TheRX service play thread, a member posted that Marco D'Angelo went 5 and 0 in March on his 5% plays and was 45 and 23 on them over 25 months, and another post reposted one of his 5% plays. The wording matches WagerTalk promotion, and the posts do not describe buying the picks.

TheRX posting rules list Marco D'Angelo, and all WagerTalk cappers, among services members should not post in its daily threads; the forum's general guidelines thread carries the same names. The rules give no reason.

In a Sportsbook Review thread about the WagerTalk site being down, one member called its free odds screen one of the best while another called the site a tout site with a useful odds screen. Nobody mentioned Marco D'Angelo.

CapperTek lists 14 reviews of WagerTalk, the store that sells his picks. The 13 with text are negative: buyers describe losing packages, records and streaks they found misleading, and one in July 2026 said reward points were hard to use because packages are always framed as discounts. None names Marco D'Angelo, so they describe the store, not him.

Web searches found no Covers or Sportsbook Review buyer thread about his paid picks, no news coverage of the 2010 baseball streak, and no court or regulator record. BBB searches for WagerTalk found no business profile. Live Reddit archive searches for his name timed out.

conflicts: WagerTalk's own 2018 and 2019 press releases call him a co founder of WagerTalk. WagerTalk grades his picks, ranks him against its other sellers, and earns money on every sale. The scorekeeper and the store are the same company, and he helped start it.

StatSalt sells the same packages at the same prices, and in August 2025 WagerTalk Media announced a partnership with PicksandParlays.net Group and WinnersAndWhiners.com. Rankings that appear across these sites are not independent confirmations of each other.
WagerTalk also owns SportsMemo, which sold his plays as recently as 17 Nov 2026. A buyer comparing "different" sites may be comparing one company's storefronts.
strengths: A public figure in Las Vegas betting media for years, named in WagerTalk's releases and on its podcasts.
Prices for every package are published, from $39 for one day to $1,999 for a year, with frequent specials.
A Last 20 list with dates, lines and results is shown on his profile, including losses and a no play.
Recent seller graded form is good: 13 and 6 over his last 20 and first on WagerTalk's 7 day all sports board on 20 Nov 2026.
We found no complaints about billing, refunds or conduct naming him.
concerns: No full public record from an outside tracker. Every ranking is WagerTalk's own, and we could not open any long term board.
He is a co founder of the company that ranks him and sells his picks.
Seller figures move: the 5% plays appear roughly even since April 2026 against a 61.7% headline, and the same 7 day record showed $1,887 on one site and $1,787 on another.
The guarantee costs extra and pays credit, not cash, and covers daily packages only.
Many prices are shown as permanent specials against a higher regular price, which makes the real price hard to judge.
His plays are on TheRX's do not post list, which limits outside tracking.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Compare the headline run with the Last 20 list and with any earlier figure for the same plays; the gap tells you how the recent stretch went.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. WagerTalk's guarantee is credit only and costs extra.
Try a 1 day or 3 day pass before a season or year pass.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, long running Las Vegas handicapper who sells through WagerTalk, a company its own press releases say he co founded. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because the only records are graded by the company that sells them, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
What does the Watchdog sample of Marco D'Angelo show?
We graded 2 of their plays that were posted publicly before the game started, 17 Oct 2026 to 24 Oct 2026: 1 won, 1 lost, -0.09 units at one unit each. That is too few plays to judge.
Is Marco D'Angelo a WagerTalk co founder?
Yes, according to WagerTalk. Its August 2018 release on buying SportsMemo quotes him as a WagerTalk co founder, and its August 2019 podcast release calls him the same. His X profile says so too.
How much does Marco D'Angelo cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 his WagerTalk profile listed passes at $39 for 1 day, $69 for 3 days, $99 for 7 days, $299 for 30 days, $749 for 90 days and $1,999 for a year ($1,188 on special). Three day sport passes were $49, and season passes ran from $259 to $719.
No cash refunds. WagerTalk sells an optional pick guarantee on daily packages that returns the paid value as account credit if the package is not profitable. Betting losses are never covered.
Does Marco D'Angelo have a verified record?
No. WagerTalk shows a Last 20 list, short leaderboards and runs such as 58 and 36 on 5% plays since 2024, all graded by WagerTalk. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.

You get plays from a veteran with published prices and a visible Last 20. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, the guarantee never returns cash, and nothing covers your betting losses.
